In few-shot use, a few solved examples are added to the prompt, and the model infers the format of the task from them. The model's parameters do not change; learning happens only within that prompt.

gl.sifir-atisli-ogrenme.why.en: It largely removes the need to retrain a model for every new task. A small number of good examples noticeably improves results, especially when a specific output format or style is required.

gl.sizma-testi.def.en: The authorized practice of probing a system for security vulnerabilities using the same methods a real attacker would use.

gl.sizma-testi.example.en: Testing, with authorization, whether the login form of a company's web application can be abused is a penetration test.

gl.sizma-testi.faq.0.a.en: It is legal when performed with the system owner's written permission and within the agreed scope. Tests carried out without permission can constitute a crime.

gl.sizma-testi.faq.1.a.en: AI tools help security teams with code review, vulnerability scanning and test scenario generation. Because attackers can use the same capabilities, the topic is controversial.

gl.sizma-testi.faq.1.q.en: How is AI used in penetration testing?

gl.sizma-testi.how.en: In a penetration test, security experts attack a website, application or network the way a real attacker would, with the permission of the system's owner. The goal is to find and report vulnerabilities before malicious actors do. Tests are conducted within a defined scope and set of rules.

gl.sizma-testi.why.en: AI agents can now automate parts of penetration testing, which makes security testing faster and cheaper. Because the same capabilities can also be used maliciously, the area is being watched closely.

gl.sohbet-botu.def.en: Software that can converse with a user in natural language, in writing or by voice. Current chatbots are based on large language models.

gl.sohbet-botu.example.en: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini are general-purpose chatbots; the digital assistant in a bank's app is a chatbot customized for a specific job.

gl.sohbet-botu.faq.0.a.en: Chatbot is a combination of the English words chat and bot; in Turkish it is used as sohbet botu. It is software that communicates with a user by typing or speaking.

gl.sohbet-botu.faq.1.a.en: It depends on the job. Different bots can stand out in tasks such as writing, coding, research and images; the most reliable approach is to try a few of them on your own work.

gl.sohbet-botu.how.en: Older chatbots worked with pre-written question-and-answer templates and got stuck on questions outside those templates. Today's chatbots are based on large language models: they read the user's message and the conversation history and generate a new response. Companies can connect these bots to their own documents (RAG) so that they can answer questions specific to their products.

gl.sohbet-botu.why.en: It is the most widespread AI application for 24/7 customer service support, quick access to information and assistance with everyday tasks. Because of the risk of giving incorrect information, human oversight is still needed on critical matters.

gl.surekli-ogrenme.def: An approach in which a model learns new data and tasks one after another over time without losing what it learned earlier, aiming for something like human lifelong learning.
gl.surekli-ogrenme.example: A spam filter has to learn new phishing tricks as they appear without losing its ability to spot the older ones.
gl.surekli-ogrenme.faq.0.a: They are close but not identical. Online learning describes data arriving as a stream with the model updated continuously. Continual learning focuses specifically on keeping old knowledge intact while new tasks arrive.
gl.surekli-ogrenme.faq.0.q: Is continual learning the same as online learning?
gl.surekli-ogrenme.faq.1.a: It is when a neural network updates its weights for a new task and in doing so disrupts the settings that worked for an earlier task, so its performance on that earlier task drops.
gl.surekli-ogrenme.how: A classic model is trained once and then frozen. If training simply continues on new data, the model can quickly forget the old material, a problem known as catastrophic forgetting. Continual learning methods try to prevent this. Examples include storing small samples from earlier tasks and replaying them, limiting changes to the weights that matter most, or reserving a separate part of the network for each task. The goal is to add new knowledge while keeping the old.
gl.surekli-ogrenme.why: The real world does not stand still: user habits, language and fraud tactics keep changing, and retraining a model from scratch each time is costly. Continual learning could reduce that cost, but forgetting remains an open research problem, and large models are still mostly updated through retraining or fine-tuning.
gl.temel-model.def: A general-purpose AI model trained at large scale on broad and varied data, which can then be adapted to many different jobs such as chat, translation, coding or image understanding.
gl.temel-model.example: A company can use the same language model under three separate products: a customer service chatbot, a contract summarizer and a coding assistant.
gl.temel-model.faq.0.a: Every large language model can be considered a foundation model, but not every foundation model is a language model; there are also ones that work with images, audio or several data types at once.
gl.temel-model.faq.0.q: Is a foundation model the same as a large language model?
gl.temel-model.faq.1.a: A foundation model is defined by being general-purpose and adaptable. A frontier model is one at the leading edge of capability at a given time; frontier models are usually foundation models as well.
gl.temel-model.faq.1.q: What is the difference between a foundation model and a frontier model?
gl.temel-model.how: A foundation model is first pretrained on internet-scale data such as text, images, audio or code, usually through self-supervised learning. This stage takes enormous computing power and gives the model broad knowledge of language and the world. The resulting model is not built for one particular job; through fine-tuning, prompting or further training it becomes the base for many different applications. It is called a foundation because many products rest on a model trained once.
gl.temel-model.why: Most of the large language models in the news are foundation models. Having one model underpin many products lowers costs, but it also means that errors and biases can carry over to all of those products. In regulatory debates, these models are often treated as a category of their own.

gl.token.def.en: The small units language models use to process text; a token can be a word or part of a word. API prices are usually set per million tokens.

gl.token.example.en: An API price of "$1.50 per million input tokens" is the fee paid for every million tokens of text sent to the model.

gl.token.faq.0.a.en: It varies by language. In English, a word averages around one token; in agglutinative languages such as Turkish, a word is often split into more than one token.

gl.token.faq.0.q.en: How many tokens is a word?

gl.token.faq.1.a.en: API fees, the context window limit and response time all depend on the number of tokens.

gl.token.faq.1.q.en: Why does the token count matter?

gl.token.how.en: Language models process text not directly as letters or words but in pieces called tokens. Common words may be a single token, while rare words are split into several pieces. In agglutinative languages such as Turkish, a single word often takes up more than one token.

gl.token.why.en: API pricing, the context window and model speed are all measured in tokens. Because the same content can take more tokens in Turkish than in English, using Turkish can be somewhat more expensive.

gl.tpu-npu.def.en: Processors designed specifically for AI computations. The TPU is the chip Google uses in its data centers; an NPU is the unit that runs AI tasks in phones and computers.

gl.tpu-npu.example.en: Tasks such as removing an object from a photo or transcribing a voice note on a phone can be done on the NPU without going online.

gl.tpu-npu.faq.0.a.en: A GPU is a general-purpose processor that can be used for graphics and many different computations. A TPU is a chip Google designed specifically for AI computations and can be more efficient for those workloads.

gl.tpu-npu.faq.0.q.en: What is the difference between a TPU and a GPU?

gl.tpu-npu.faq.1.a.en: Some AI features (such as image editing, live captions and noise cancellation) can run faster and with less battery use, without sending data to cloud servers.

gl.tpu-npu.faq.1.q.en: What is the benefit of having an NPU in my computer?

gl.tpu-npu.how.en: GPUs are general-purpose parallel processors suited to many different computations. TPUs and NPUs are designed specifically to perform large matrix multiplications, the core operation of AI, with less energy. Google uses TPUs in its own data centers to train and run its models and also rents them to cloud customers. NPUs are built into phone and laptop processors.

gl.tpu-npu.why.en: Because demand for AI chips has increased dependence on Nvidia's GPUs, big tech companies are developing their own chips. NPUs allow AI to run on the device itself, without an internet connection and more privately.

gl.transfer-ogrenme.def: Reusing the knowledge a model gained on one task for a related task, so that work on the new problem starts from an existing foundation rather than from scratch.
gl.transfer-ogrenme.example: A hospital can take a model trained on general image datasets and adapt it with only a few thousand X-rays to build a system that flags abnormalities in chest scans.
gl.transfer-ogrenme.faq.0.a: Fine-tuning is a common way of doing transfer learning: the weights of a pretrained model are updated with new data. Transfer learning is the broader idea and covers any way of carrying knowledge over to another task.
gl.transfer-ogrenme.faq.0.q: What is the difference between transfer learning and fine-tuning?
gl.transfer-ogrenme.faq.1.a: No. If the source and target tasks are very different, the transferred knowledge may not help and can even make results worse.
gl.transfer-ogrenme.how: A model is first trained on a broad dataset, for example learning to recognize objects from millions of images. Its weights are then used as the starting point for a new task. Either only the last layers are trained on the new data, or the whole model is fine-tuned with small updates. Because the lower layers already know general features such as edges, textures or language patterns, the new task needs far less data. Someone who plays piano picking up the organ faster is a fair analogy.
gl.transfer-ogrenme.why: Many organizations lack the data or computing power to train a large model from nothing. Transfer learning lets them adapt ready-made models to specialized jobs with little data and at low cost. The common practice of fine-tuning pretrained models today is a direct result of this approach.

gl.transformer.def.en: A neural network architecture introduced in 2017 that uses an "attention" mechanism to evaluate the relationships among all the words in a text at once. Nearly all large language models are based on this architecture.

gl.transformer.example.en: Models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Llama all use different variants of the transformer architecture; the architecture has also become widespread in image and audio models.

gl.transformer.faq.0.a.en: GPT is the abbreviation of generative pre-trained transformer; the T stands for the transformer architecture.

gl.transformer.faq.0.q.en: What does the T in GPT stand for?

gl.transformer.faq.1.a.en: It is the method that calculates how much importance a model should give to which other words in the text while processing a given word. It forms the basis of understanding context.

gl.transformer.how.en: The transformer uses the "attention" mechanism to calculate how related each word in a sentence is to every other word. This lets it determine the meaning of a word like "bank" in a sentence such as "He sat on the bank" by looking at the surrounding words. Unlike older methods, it processes text in parallel rather than word by word in sequence, which allows very large models to be trained efficiently on GPUs.

gl.transformer.why.en: Introduced in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" by Google researchers, this architecture forms the foundation of today's large language models. The "T" in GPT also comes from transformer.

gl.turing-testi.def.en: A thought experiment proposed by Alan Turing in 1950 that measures whether a machine can behave so much like a human in written conversation that it cannot be told apart from one.

gl.turing-testi.example.en: A user being unable to tell whether the party they are chatting with in customer service is a human or a bot is an everyday reflection of the Turing test.

gl.turing-testi.faq.0.a.en: Some studies have reported that current language models can convince a significant share of participants that they are human in short conversations. However, results depend on how the test is set up, and the test's value for measuring intelligence is disputed.

gl.turing-testi.faq.0.q.en: Has ChatGPT passed the Turing test?

gl.turing-testi.faq.1.a.en: He was a British mathematician and one of the founders of computer science. He proposed the Turing test in his 1950 paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence."

gl.turing-testi.how.en: In the test, an evaluator converses in writing only with two parties, one human and one machine, and tries to work out which is the machine. If the evaluator cannot reliably tell the machine apart, the machine is considered to have passed. Turing proposed this as a measurable question to replace "Can machines think?"

gl.turing-testi.why.en: It is one of the best-known benchmarks in artificial intelligence. As today's language models can write in a human-like way, the meaning of the test is being debated again: many researchers argue that being able to imitate a human does not show real intelligence or understanding.

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.def.en: AI that can produce new text, images, audio, video or code based on the examples it has learned from. ChatGPT and image-generating models fall into this category.

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.example.en: A chat assistant that writes an email, a tool that creates a poster image from a single sentence and models that produce video from a short text are examples of generative AI.

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.faq.0.a.en: Classical systems generally classify or predict (is this email spam?). Generative AI, on the other hand, creates new content (write a reply to this email).

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.faq.0.q.en: What is the difference between generative AI and classical AI?

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.faq.1.a.en: No. Models can produce fluent but incorrect information (hallucination). Important information should always be verified against a reliable source.

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.faq.1.q.en: Is content produced by generative AI always accurate?

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.how.en: Generative models learn patterns in their training data and produce new content that fits those patterns. Language models generate text by predicting the most likely next word in a passage; image models typically start from noise and build a meaningful picture step by step. The user describes what they want with a prompt.

gl.uretken-yapay-zeka.why.en: It cuts creative work that only humans could do before, such as writing, design, coding, music and video, down to minutes. While this boosts productivity, it also raises new debates over copyright, fake content and the effects on professions.

gl.uzman-sistem.def: A computer program that stores a human expert's knowledge as rules and uses it to answer questions or recommend decisions in a specific field. Expert systems became widespread in the 1970s and 1980s.
gl.uzman-sistem.example: MYCIN, developed at Stanford University in the 1970s, was a well-known research prototype that used a set of rules to suggest which antibiotic to give for blood infections.
gl.uzman-sistem.faq.0.a: In an expert system, people write the rules; in machine learning, the model learns from examples. That makes expert systems easy to trace but laborious to keep up to date.
gl.uzman-sistem.faq.0.q: What is the difference between an expert system and machine learning?
gl.uzman-sistem.faq.1.a: They are less often called by that name, but rule-based decision support and automation software is still used at many organizations.
gl.uzman-sistem.how: An expert system has three main parts: a knowledge base that holds the rules, an inference engine that chains those rules together to reach a conclusion, and an interface for talking to the user. Knowledge engineers interview the expert and write rules like “if this symptom is present, this diagnosis becomes more likely”. As the user answers questions, the engine fires the relevant rules in sequence and produces a recommendation. It can often also show which rules led to that result.
gl.uzman-sistem.why: Expert systems were among the first serious commercial uses of AI and drew heavy corporate investment in the 1980s. But the difficulty of keeping the rules up to date and their brittleness in unforeseen situations contributed to disappointed expectations and, eventually, an AI winter. They can be seen as ancestors of today's rule-based decision software.

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.def.en: An architecture in which a model consists of many sub-networks (experts) and only a few of them run for each input. It makes it possible to run large models at lower compute cost.

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.example.en: A model with 600 billion total parameters, of which about 30 billion run for each token, is an example of a mixture-of-experts architecture.

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.faq.0.a.en: It is the number of parameters actually used when processing a token in mixture-of-experts models. Speed and compute cost depend largely on active parameters.

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.faq.1.a.en: No. Generally, all experts need to be kept ready in memory. The savings come not from memory but from the amount of computation performed at each step.

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.faq.1.q.en: Do MoE models use less memory?

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.how.en: In a mixture-of-experts model, some of the layers consist of many parallel sub-networks (experts). A router selects only a few of these experts for each token. So even if the model's total parameter count is very large, only a small fraction of them runs at each step.

gl.uzmanlar-karisimi.why.en: It makes it possible to build models that carry more knowledge at lower compute cost. Many current open-weight models use this architecture, which is why model cards distinguish between "total parameters" and "active parameters."

gl.vektor-veritabani.def.en: A database that stores embedding vectors and makes it possible to quickly find the content most similar in meaning. It is used in document search and RAG systems.

gl.vektor-veritabani.example.en: A law firm can load thousands of contracts into a vector database and quickly find relevant documents with queries such as "lease agreements with a termination clause."

gl.vektor-veritabani.faq.0.a.en: Regular databases search by exact match or specific values. Vector databases calculate the proximity between vectors to find content that is similar in meaning.

gl.vektor-veritabani.faq.0.q.en: What is the difference between a vector database and a regular database?

gl.vektor-veritabani.faq.1.a.en: No. If there are only a few documents, all of them can be given directly to the model. For large, constantly updated document archives, a vector database is more efficient.

gl.vektor-veritabani.faq.1.q.en: Is a vector database necessary for every AI project?

gl.vektor-veritabani.how.en: Documents are first split into chunks, and each chunk is converted into a vector by an embedding model. The vector database stores these vectors. When a user asks a question, the question is also converted into a vector, and the database finds the document chunks closest in meaning within milliseconds. The retrieved chunks are then given to the language model as context.

gl.vektor-veritabani.why.en: It is a core building block for companies to build AI assistants that give current, accurate answers based on their own documents. It makes it possible to add new information without retraining the model.

gl.veri-merkezi.def.en: A facility where thousands of servers and storage and networking equipment operate together. AI models are trained and run on GPUs in these facilities.

gl.veri-merkezi.example.en: A company announcing that it is building a "200 MW AI data center" is a typical infrastructure news item.

gl.veri-merkezi.faq.0.a.en: Thousands of GPUs run at high power at the same time and require intensive cooling. That is why the electricity consumption of large AI data centers is compared to that of small cities.

gl.veri-merkezi.faq.0.q.en: Why do AI data centers consume so much energy?

gl.veri-merkezi.faq.1.a.en: Turkey has a number of data centers, and investment plans for AI infrastructure are being announced; you can follow the latest developments in our Turkey section.

gl.veri-merkezi.faq.1.q.en: Are there AI data centers in Turkey?

gl.veri-merkezi.how.en: Data centers are facilities that house thousands of servers, storage systems and the networking equipment that connects them. AI data centers need very high electrical power and advanced cooling systems to run large numbers of GPUs together. Their capacity is usually expressed in megawatts (MW).

gl.veri-merkezi.why.en: Because AI models are trained and used in data centers, investment in these facilities has reached record levels. Their energy consumption, water use and which countries they are built in are also the subject of major policy debates.

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.def.en: A mathematical model, inspired by the neurons in the brain, that consists of many simple computing units in interconnected layers and learns from data.

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.example.en: A small neural network that recognizes handwritten digits is often used as the first example in AI courses.

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.faq.0.a.en: It is only loosely inspired by it. Artificial neural networks consist of mathematical calculations and are a highly simplified model of the biological processes in the brain.

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.faq.0.q.en: Does an artificial neural network work like the human brain?

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.faq.1.a.en: The weights of the connections in a neural network are the model's parameters. For example, a model with 70 billion parameters has that many adjustable values.

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.faq.1.q.en: What is the relationship between parameters and a neural network?

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.how.en: A neural network consists of an input layer, one or more hidden layers and an output layer. Each unit multiplies the numbers it receives by certain weights, sums them and passes the result to the next layer. During training, the network's prediction is compared with the correct answer, and the weights are updated backward to reduce the error (backpropagation).

gl.yapay-sinir-agi.why.en: Neural networks are the building blocks of deep learning and, by extension, of today's language, image and audio models. What we call a model's "parameter count" is the number of weights in this network.

gl.yapay-super-zeka.def: A theoretical level of AI that would far surpass human intelligence in nearly every field, including scientific creativity and general reasoning. No such system exists today.
gl.yapay-super-zeka.example: A single system that designs new drugs, solves physics problems and runs a company far better than the best human experts would count as ASI, but for now that remains science fiction.
gl.yapay-super-zeka.faq.0.a: AGI describes a system that can do a broad range of tasks at a human level. Superintelligence would go beyond that level and be far more capable than any human.
gl.yapay-super-zeka.faq.0.q: What is the difference between superintelligence and artificial general intelligence (AGI)?
gl.yapay-super-zeka.faq.1.a: Nobody knows. Experts' estimates range from several decades to never, so anyone offering a firm timeline deserves some skepticism.
gl.yapay-super-zeka.how: Since superintelligence is still hypothetical, how it would work is not settled; the discussion usually treats it as a stage after artificial general intelligence. One scenario goes like this: a system that reaches human level improves its own design, the improved system does so even faster, and progress quickly leaves humans behind. Other researchers consider such a rapid leap unlikely and expect progress to be slow, gradual, or held back by limits in hardware, data and energy.
gl.yapay-super-zeka.why: Superintelligence sits at the center of debates about AI safety and alignment. Some people regard it as a serious long-term risk that warrants precautions today; others think the focus distracts from present-day problems such as bias and effects on jobs. Knowing this divide helps when reading news claims about it.

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.def.en: An AI system that carries out a given goal by planning the steps itself and using tools, such as searching the web, filling in forms or running code.

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.example.en: Systems that search for restaurants and make reservations on a user's behalf, or complete an online purchase after getting approval, are AI agents.

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.faq.0.a.en: A chatbot answers questions. An agent uses tools to do work on the user's behalf, such as searching, filling in forms, editing files or shopping.

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.faq.0.q.en: What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.faq.1.a.en: It depends on the authority they are given. Requiring approval for important actions, limiting the agent's access and tracking what it does reduce the risks.

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.how.en: An AI agent combines a language model with tools: it can search the web, read files, fill in forms, run code or use other applications. It breaks the goal it is given into steps, decides on the next one by looking at the result of each step, and continues until the job is done.

gl.yapay-zeka-ajani.why.en: Agents turn AI from an assistant that only answers questions into a colleague that does work on the user's behalf. They are spreading quickly in areas such as shopping, appointment booking, software development and customer service, and questions about security and accountability come with them.

gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.def: A period in which unmet, overblown expectations cause interest, investment and research funding for AI to drop sharply. The term describes the boom-and-bust pattern in the field's history.
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.example: In the 1980s, companies selling expert systems and firms building specialized AI computers such as Lisp machines lost customers and saw their market shrink as cheaper general-purpose computers rose.
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.faq.0.a: People usually speak of two major ones, in the 1970s and in the late 1980s. Historians do not agree on their exact boundaries, and smaller downturns are also mentioned.
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.faq.0.q: How many AI winters have there been?
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.faq.1.a: Nobody can say for sure. Some commentators think inflated expectations could cause another letdown; others argue that real, widespread use of today's technology makes this period unlike the earlier ones.
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.faq.1.q: Will there be another AI winter?
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.how: The cycle tends to run the same way: a new method brings big promises, money flows in, results fall short of expectations, disappointment sets in and funding is cut. History usually points to two major winters: roughly the 1970s, and the stretch from the late 1980s into the early 1990s. In the second, the collapse of the expert system market and of the market for specialized hardware played a part. Research never stopped completely during these winters; many ideas kept developing in a quieter climate.
gl.yapay-zeka-kisi.why: The term often comes up when today's wave of AI investment is discussed. One view holds that inflated expectations could lead to another downturn; another says things are different now because today's systems are actually used by large numbers of people. History cannot predict the future, but it is a useful reminder about managing expectations.

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.def.en: When an AI system systematically produces erroneous or unfair results against certain people or groups. It mostly stems from imbalances in the training data.

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.example.en: A résumé-screening system trained on data in which mostly male candidates were hired in the past may systematically score female candidates lower.

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.faq.0.a.en: The main methods are diversifying the training data, testing results separately for different groups, auditing decisions regularly and keeping human oversight in critical decisions.

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.faq.0.q.en: How can AI bias be reduced?

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.faq.1.a.en: Building a completely unbiased system is very difficult, because data and definitions come from people. The goal is to measure bias, be transparent and minimize its harmful effects.

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.how.en: When certain groups are underrepresented in the training data or the data contains past discriminatory decisions, a model learns and repeats these imbalances. Bias can arise from data collection, labeling, the model's design or the way it is used.

gl.yapay-zeka-onyargisi.why.en: In areas that affect people's lives, such as hiring, credit assessment, healthcare and security, biased decisions can lead to serious injustices. That is why regulations such as the EU AI Act impose data quality and oversight requirements on high-risk systems.

gl.yapay-zeka.def.en: The general name for technologies that enable computers to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, understanding language, seeing and making decisions.

gl.yapay-zeka.example.en: Your phone's face unlock, the spam filter in your email, a navigation app's traffic predictions and chat assistants such as ChatGPT are examples of AI in daily life.

gl.yapay-zeka.faq.0.a.en: No. Artificial intelligence is the name of the overall field; machine learning is today's most common way of achieving AI. Deep learning is a subfield of machine learning.

gl.yapay-zeka.faq.0.q.en: Are artificial intelligence and machine learning the same thing?

gl.yapay-zeka.faq.1.a.en: Today's AI systems do not think consciously like humans; they make predictions and generate output based on the patterns they have learned. Although they surpass human level on some tasks, they can make simple mistakes on others.

gl.yapay-zeka.how.en: Artificial intelligence is not a single technology but an umbrella term for many methods. Older systems ran on rules written one by one by people; most of today's systems use machine learning to learn patterns in large datasets on their own. A language model learns the structure of language from billions of sentences, and an image model learns what objects look like from millions of photos, then applies that knowledge to new inputs.

gl.yapay-zeka.why.en: It is changing the way business is done in nearly every sector, from search engines to banking, healthcare to advertising. Alongside opportunities such as productivity gains, new products and a transformation of the labor market, it brings risks such as misinformation, privacy and security; for this reason, governments are drafting laws to regulate AI.

gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.def: A machine learning approach that trains a model using a small amount of labeled data together with a large amount of unlabeled data. It sits between supervised and unsupervised learning.
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.example: A hospital might have radiologists label only a few hundred X-rays, then add thousands of unlabeled X-rays to training in the hope of getting a better model.
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.faq.0.a: Semi-supervised learning has at least a few labeled examples, and the model learns its target from them. Unsupervised learning has no labels at all.
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.faq.0.q: What is the difference between semi-supervised and unsupervised learning?
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.faq.1.a: No. If its assumptions fail, for example if the unlabeled data differs from the labeled data, results can get worse, so the method is not helpful for every problem.
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.faq.1.q: Does semi-supervised learning always give better results?
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.how: The process starts with an initial model trained on a small labeled set. The structure of the unlabeled data then comes into play, drawing on assumptions such as the tendency of similar examples to share the same label. In one common method, the model makes predictions on unlabeled examples, treats the ones it is confident about as provisional labels, and retrains itself on the enlarged dataset. This lets most of the costly labeling work be skipped.
gl.yari-denetimli-ogrenme.why: Producing labels often takes expert effort; for instance, only doctors can label medical images correctly. Semi-supervised learning promises to cut that cost. Still, if a model treats its own wrong predictions as labels, errors can reinforce themselves, so careful validation is needed.

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.def.en: A model reasoning by writing out intermediate steps in order instead of jumping straight to a conclusion. It improves accuracy on math and logic questions.

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.example.en: Given the question "A product costs 240 lira after a 20% discount; what was the price before the discount?", the model first writing that 240 is 80% of the price and then arriving at 300 lira is chain-of-thought.

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.faq.0.a.en: It can improve accuracy on multi-step questions, especially in models without reasoning capabilities. Reasoning models already do this internally, so they need additional instructions less.

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.faq.0.q.en: Does saying "think step by step" really work?

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.faq.1.a.en: Not always. Research shows that the rationale a model writes may not always fully reflect how it actually arrived at its decision.

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.faq.1.q.en: Are the thinking steps a model writes always genuine?

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.how.en: The model is asked to write out intermediate steps, either with an instruction such as "think step by step" or by showing example solutions. Because the model uses the result of the previous step at each step, it effectively breaks a complex problem into small pieces. Reasoning models carry out this thinking process on their own, before the answer.

gl.zincirleme-dusunce.why.en: It noticeably improves accuracy on multi-step math, logic and planning questions. Seeing the intermediate steps also makes it easier to understand where the model went wrong.

task.muzik-yapma.intro.en: Tools that generate songs with vocals and background music from a prompt or lyrics. Commercial use rights are usually granted only on paid plans.

task.muzik-yapma.pick.elevenlabs.en: Music generation alongside voiceover and sound effects.

task.muzik-yapma.pick.suno.en: The most widely used tool for generating songs with vocals; commercial use is on paid plans.

task.muzik-yapma.title.en: Best AI tools for making music and songs

task.ozet-cikarma.intro.en: Tools that summarize PDFs, articles, reports and videos.

task.ozet-cikarma.pick.chatgpt.en: Upload files and get summaries in different formats.

task.ozet-cikarma.pick.claude.en: Can read very long documents in their entirety.

task.ozet-cikarma.pick.notebooklm.en: Summaries and Q&A based on the documents you upload.

task.ozet-cikarma.pick.perplexity.en: Sourced summaries of a topic from the web.

task.seslendirme.intro.en: Tools that turn text into natural human-sounding speech, clone voices and dub videos into other languages.

task.seslendirme.pick.elevenlabs.en: Multilingual, natural text-to-speech and voice cloning, including Turkish.

task.seslendirme.pick.heygen.en: For translating a video into another language and dubbing it in the same voice.

task.seslendirme.pick.microsoft-copilot.en: Audio summaries and read-aloud features within Office.

task.sohbet.intro.en: General-purpose assistants used for asking questions, drafting text, summarizing and generating ideas. All of them understand Turkish; the differences lie mostly in the tasks they are strongest at, integrations and usage limits.

task.sohbet.pick.chatgpt.en: The broadest feature set: image generation, file analysis, agents and voice in a single app.

task.sohbet.pick.claude.en: Strong at long documents, quality writing and coding.

task.sohbet.pick.deepseek.en: A free and powerful alternative; pay attention to its privacy policy.

task.sohbet.pick.perplexity.en: For up-to-date information with linked sources.

task.sohbet.title.en: Best AI assistants for chat and everyday tasks

task.sunum-hazirlama.intro.en: Tools that generate slides from a topic or text, or help structure the flow of a presentation.

task.sunum-hazirlama.pick.chatgpt.en: Presentation ideas, flow and image generation.

task.sunum-hazirlama.pick.claude.en: For presentation flow, slide text and speaker notes.

task.sunum-hazirlama.pick.gamma.en: For generating a designed slide deck from text.

task.sunum-hazirlama.title.en: Best AI tools for creating presentations

task.toplanti-notu.intro.en: Tools that transcribe meetings and produce summaries and task lists. Participants must be informed before recording.

task.toplanti-notu.pick.fireflies.en: Sends meeting summaries to your work tools.

task.toplanti-notu.pick.otter.en: Automatic notes and summaries for English-language meetings.

task.toplanti-notu.title.en: Best AI tools for meeting notes

task.video-olusturma.intro.en: Tools that generate video from text or images and produce presentation videos with avatars. Most run on a credit system; costs rise quickly as video length increases.

task.video-olusturma.pick.gemini.en: Google's video models are offered in Gemini plans.

task.video-olusturma.pick.runway.en: Creative short videos and video editing.

task.video-olusturma.title.en: Best AI tools for creating videos

task.yapay-zeka-dedektoru.intro.en: Tools that try to estimate whether a text was written by AI. Important warning: No detection tool gives definitive results; they can be wrong, especially on Turkish and edited text.

task.yapay-zeka-dedektoru.pick.gptzero.en: One of the most widely used detection tools; its result should not be treated as proof on its own.

task.yapay-zeka-dedektoru.title.en: AI detectors: text detection tools and their limits

tool.adobe-firefly.desc.en: Adobe's AI tool that generates images, video and audio. It integrates with Photoshop and other Adobe apps; Adobe says it trains its own models on licensed content.

tool.adobe-firefly.good.0.en: Those who work with Photoshop and Adobe apps

tool.adobe-firefly.good.1.en: Agencies and brands that value assurances for commercial use

tool.adobe-firefly.notFor.0.en: The credit system may feel complicated for those who don't use the Adobe ecosystem

tool.canva.desc.en: A template-based online design tool. Its AI features (Magic Studio) offer text-to-image generation and automatic editing for social media graphics, presentations, posters and logo design.

tool.canva.good.0.en: Creating social media posts, presentations and posters without design expertise

tool.canva.notFor.1.en: More specialized tools exist for those who only want to generate AI images

tool.capcut.desc.en: Video editing app from ByteDance, TikTok's owner. Speeds up short video production with auto captions, background removal, text-to-video and AI effects.

tool.capcut.good.0.en: Quick short videos for Reels, TikTok and Shorts

tool.capcut.notFor.1.en: Those who want a fixed price: amounts vary by region, and the final price is shown after sign-in

tool.capcut.plan.1.note.en: AI features and 1,200 credits per month; 7-day trial for new users

tool.chatgpt.desc.en: OpenAI's general-purpose AI assistant. It offers writing, analysis, coding, image generation, file reading and web search in a single app, and is the most widely used chat assistant in the world.

tool.chatgpt.good.0.en: All kinds of everyday writing, summarizing and idea generation

tool.chatgpt.good.1.en: People who want image generation, file analysis and other tasks in one place

tool.chatgpt.good.2.en: A broad ecosystem of plugins, agents and integrations

tool.chatgpt.notFor.0.en: Research where source citation and up-to-date information matter above all (use alongside tools with web search)

tool.chatgpt.notFor.1.en: Work where data must not leave the company (requires an enterprise plan or a local model)

tool.claude.desc.en: Anthropic's AI assistant. It stands out for working with long documents, quality writing, analysis and coding; with Claude Code, it gives developers a coding agent that runs in the terminal and editor.

tool.claude.good.0.en: Reading and analyzing long reports, contracts and documents

tool.claude.good.1.en: Careful, natural Turkish and English writing

tool.claude.notFor.0.en: Generating images (Claude does not generate images; it reads and interprets them)

tool.claude.notFor.1.en: With very heavy use, free plan limits can feel tight

tool.cursor.desc.en: An AI-powered code editor developed by Anysphere and acquired by SpaceX in 2026. It offers code writing and editing with models from different companies, plus agent features that make changes across an entire project.

tool.cursor.good.1.en: Working with AI on large codebases

tool.cursor.good.2.en: Trying different models in a single editor

tool.cursor.notFor.0.en: People with no coding knowledge (basic programming or a chat assistant is recommended first)

tool.deepl.desc.en: A Germany-based AI translation tool. It offers text and document translation in dozens of languages, including Turkish, as well as writing improvement (DeepL Write).

tool.deepl.good.1.en: Translating Word and PDF documents while preserving formatting

tool.deepl.notFor.0.en: Documents requiring official or sworn translation

tool.deepseek.desc.en: The chat assistant and open-weight models from China's DeepSeek. The web and mobile chat app is offered free; the models also stand out for their low API prices.

tool.deepseek.good.0.en: People looking for a free and powerful assistant

tool.deepseek.good.2.en: Developers who want to run an open-weight model on their own servers

tool.deepseek.notFor.0.en: Work involving personal or company data: data may be processed on servers in China; review the privacy policy

tool.deepseek.notFor.1.en: May decline to answer on some political topics

tool.deepseek.priceNote.en: The chat app is free; see our model comparison table for API prices.

tool.elevenlabs.desc.en: An AI platform that turns text into natural-sounding human speech, with voice cloning and voiceover. Offers multilingual voiceover, dubbing and voice assistant infrastructure.

tool.elevenlabs.good.0.en: Voiceover for video, podcasts and e-learning

tool.elevenlabs.good.2.en: Cloning your own voice to create content

tool.elevenlabs.notFor.0.en: Cloning someone else's voice without permission (legally and ethically problematic)

tool.fireflies.desc.en: An AI note-taking tool that joins and records online meetings and produces transcripts, summaries and task lists.

tool.fireflies.good.0.en: Sharing meeting notes with the team

tool.fireflies.good.1.en: Sending meeting summaries to CRM and project tools

tool.fireflies.notFor.0.en: Recording without participant consent (always inform attendees)

tool.gamma.desc.en: An AI tool that generates presentations, documents and web pages from text or an outline. It creates slides in minutes with ready-made designs.

tool.gamma.good.1.en: Good-looking slides without fussing over design

tool.gamma.notFor.0.en: Presentations that must match a corporate template exactly (final editing required)

tool.gamma.priceNote.en: Free, Plus, Pro, Ultra and Business plans are available; a 28% discount applies to annual billing (Gamma help page). Check the official page for current pricing.

tool.gemini.desc.en: Google's AI assistant. It integrates with Google services such as Gmail, Docs, Drive and YouTube, and offers image and video generation, long-document analysis and research features.

tool.gemini.good.0.en: Heavy users of Google accounts (Gmail, Drive, Docs)

tool.gemini.good.2.en: People who want to use image and video generation together with an assistant

tool.gemini.notFor.0.en: The integration advantage shrinks for those who don't use the Google ecosystem

tool.github-copilot.desc.en: GitHub's AI coding assistant. It offers code completion, chat and coding agent features in VS Code, JetBrains and other editors.

tool.github-copilot.good.0.en: Those who want to add AI without changing their current editor

tool.github-copilot.notFor.0.en: Those looking for a general-purpose assistant outside the editor

tool.google-translate.desc.en: Google's free translation service. It can translate text, documents, websites, speech and camera input in real time, with very broad language support.

tool.google-translate.good.1.en: Camera and voice translation while traveling

tool.google-translate.notFor.0.en: Marketing and literary texts where tone and style matter

tool.gptzero.desc.en: A detection tool that estimates the likelihood that a text was written with AI. It is widely used among educators.

tool.gptzero.good.0.en: Getting a first impression of a text

tool.gptzero.notFor.0.en: Accusations or grading decisions on its own (detection tools can be wrong; see our guide)

tool.gptzero.notFor.1.en: Turkish texts: results may be less reliable

tool.grammarly.desc.en: AI writing assistant that offers spelling, grammar, tone and clarity suggestions for English texts. Works in emails, documents and messages via its browser extension and apps.

tool.grammarly.good.0.en: English emails, reports and application letters

tool.grammarly.good.1.en: Improving tone and clarity when writing in English

tool.grammarly.notFor.0.en: Turkish texts (the tool is designed for English writing)

tool.grammarly.plan.0.note.en: spelling correction, tone analysis, 100 AI prompts

tool.grok.desc.en: The assistant from xAI, the AI company founded by Elon Musk. It is integrated with X (Twitter) and stands out for its access to current posts on X.

tool.grok.good.0.en: Those who follow trending topics and posts on X

tool.grok.good.1.en: Those looking for fast, up-to-date information

tool.grok.notFor.0.en: Work that requires verification, since posts on X are not always accurate

tool.heygen.desc.en: An AI tool that generates talking digital avatar videos and dubs videos into different languages. Used in training, promotional and corporate communications videos.

tool.heygen.good.0.en: Presenter/avatar videos without appearing on camera

tool.heygen.good.1.en: Translating and dubbing videos into other languages

tool.heygen.notFor.0.en: Using a real person's avatar or voice without their permission (ethical and legal risk)

tool.ideogram.desc.en: An AI tool that generates images from text. Known for its success in producing legible text within images; preferred for logos, posters and typographic designs.

tool.ideogram.good.0.en: Posters, covers and logo drafts that include text

tool.ideogram.notFor.0.en: Final, ready-to-use logo designs that can be trademarked (a professional designer is needed)

tool.kickresume.desc.en: An AI-powered tool for preparing résumés and cover letters. It offers ready-made templates and AI writing suggestions.

tool.kickresume.good.0.en: A quick, polished résumé from a template

tool.kickresume.notFor.0.en: Turkish résumés: you may need to use the template and write the text yourself

tool.kling.desc.en: An AI tool from China's Kuaishou that generates video from text and images. Stands out for realistic motion and scene generation.

tool.kling.notFor.0.en: Corporate projects where data privacy is sensitive (review the policy)

tool.le-chat.desc.en: The chat assistant from France's Mistral AI. Offers web search, deep research, document analysis and image generation; stands out as a Europe-based alternative.

tool.le-chat.good.0.en: Users who prefer a Europe-based assistant

tool.le-chat.good.1.en: Those looking for an affordably priced paid plan

tool.le-chat.notFor.0.en: Turkish-heavy work: test language quality on the free plan first

tool.le-chat.plan.1.note.en: excluding taxes; $5.99 per month for verified students

tool.lovable.desc.en: Sweden-based AI tool that builds websites and apps through conversation. You describe what you want, and it generates the code and interface itself; designed for people who don't know how to code.

tool.lovable.good.0.en: Prototypes, landing pages or simple apps without coding

tool.lovable.good.1.en: Quickly turning an idea into a working version to test

tool.lovable.notFor.0.en: Large and complex software projects (a developer tool is needed)

tool.lovable.notFor.1.en: Heavy use without tracking credit consumption

tool.meta-ai.desc.en: Meta's AI assistant. Works inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, offering question answering, text writing and image generation. Available in Turkish in Turkey since October 2025.

tool.meta-ai.good.0.en: Quick Q&A inside WhatsApp or Instagram, which you already use

tool.meta-ai.good.1.en: Creating short text and images within a chat

tool.meta-ai.notFor.0.en: Long documents and in-depth analysis (general-purpose assistants are stronger)

tool.meta-ai.notFor.1.en: Sharing private personal or company information

tool.meta-ai.priceNote.en: Free; can be used inside WhatsApp and Instagram without downloading a separate app.

tool.microsoft-copilot.desc.en: Microsoft's AI assistant. Alongside the free Copilot app, it works inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook with Microsoft 365 subscriptions.

tool.microsoft-copilot.good.0.en: People who work with Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook

tool.microsoft-copilot.good.2.en: People who want to edit Office documents with AI

tool.microsoft-copilot.notFor.0.en: The paid plans offer limited advantage for those who don't use Office

tool.midjourney.desc.en: An AI tool that generates high-quality, aesthetically strong images from text. One of the best-known tools for artistic and cinematic visuals; it also offers video generation.

tool.midjourney.good.1.en: Concept design, moodboards and campaign ideas

tool.midjourney.notFor.0.en: Those who want to try it for free (there is no free plan)

tool.midjourney.notFor.1.en: Designs that need long, accurate text within the image

tool.notebooklm.desc.en: Google's research assistant that answers based on the documents you upload. It generates summaries, Q&A and audio overviews (podcast-style) from PDFs, web pages and videos.

tool.notebooklm.good.0.en: Learning from lecture notes, articles and reports

tool.notebooklm.good.1.en: Getting answers based only on your own documents

tool.notebooklm.notFor.0.en: General knowledge and web research not found in the documents

tool.notebooklm.priceNote.en: Free to use; higher limits are included in Google AI plans.

tool.notion.desc.en: AI features of Notion, the note, document and project management app. Summarizes pages, writes text, produces meeting notes and offers agents that search the workspace.

tool.notion.good.0.en: Teams that already keep their notes and documents in Notion

tool.notion.good.1.en: Meeting notes and quick access to internal company information

tool.notion.notFor.0.en: Those who don't use Notion (the AI features run inside the app)

tool.notion.plan.1.note.en: per user; Notion AI trial only

tool.otter.desc.en: An AI meeting assistant that records and transcribes meetings and produces summaries and task lists. It works with Zoom, Google Meet and Teams.

tool.otter.good.1.en: Summaries of sales and customer calls

tool.otter.notFor.0.en: Turkish-language meetings: check language support before buying

tool.perplexity.desc.en: An AI search engine that searches the web and gives its answers with source links. It is designed for up-to-date information and sourced research.

tool.perplexity.good.0.en: Up-to-date information search with source links

tool.perplexity.notFor.0.en: Long creative writing and extensive document editing

tool.perplexity.notFor.1.en: Assuming sources are always interpreted correctly (open the links and check them)

tool.runway.desc.en: A platform that generates video from text and images and offers AI tools for video editing. Widely used in advertising, film and content production.

tool.runway.good.0.en: Short ads and social media videos

tool.runway.notFor.0.en: Long videos: costs can rise quickly because of the credit system

tool.suno.desc.en: An AI music tool that generates songs with vocals from a text description or lyrics.

tool.suno.good.0.en: Quick songs and music for social media, ads and personal projects

tool.suno.good.1.en: Musicians who want to try out a song idea

tool.suno.notFor.0.en: Using songs generated on the free plan commercially (a paid plan is required)

tool.synthesia.desc.en: A London-based AI platform that generates avatar-led training and corporate videos from text. Focuses on in-house training and promotional videos.

yerli.bilge.about.en: A family of large language models ranging from 1 billion to 122 billion parameters, developed around the structure and cultural context of Turkish. According to its official website, it has not yet been opened to general use.

yerli.bilge.access.en: Not yet available for general use

yerli.cosmos.about.en: Turkish models from the COSMOS research group at YTU's Computer Engineering department. Turkish-Gemma-9b-T1 is adapted for math, logic and step-by-step reasoning in Turkish; it is offered under the Gemma license.

yerli.cosmos.access.en: Models can be downloaded from Hugging Face

yerli.evren.about.en: An end-to-end AI platform offering data labeling, model training, and image and large language model inference in one place. It runs on a credit system; credits can be earned through contributions such as data labeling.

yerli.havelsan-main.about.en: An enterprise AI platform. Alongside a 9-billion-parameter Turkish large language model, it includes open-source intelligence, image and speech models, and can be trained on organizations' own data.

yerli.havelsan-main.access.en: Aimed at organizations; runs on the organization's own servers or on a closed network

yerli.kumru.about.en: A 7.4-billion-parameter language model developed for Turkish. It was unveiled in October 2025; its smaller 2-billion-parameter version was released as open source on Hugging Face.

yerli.kumru.access.en: Chat via kumru.ai; the small version (Kumru-2B) is downloadable

yerli.t3-ai.about.en: An open-source large language model project led by the T3 Foundation, aiming to represent Turkish strongly in AI. The official page does not list a model version or access information.

yerli.t3-ai.access.en: The official page has no model download or API information

yerli.trendyol-llm.about.en: Trendyol-LLM-8B-T1 is an 8-billion-parameter model based on Qwen3-8B and fine-tuned on Trendyol's Turkish e-commerce data. It is available for commercial use under the Apache 2.0 license.

yerli.trendyol-llm.access.en: Model is downloaded from Hugging Face and run on your own hardware

yerli.turkcell-llm.about.en: Turkcell-LLM-7b-v1, a Turkish language model based on Mistral 7B. It was released under the Apache 2.0 license.

yerli.turkcell-llm.access.en: Model can be downloaded from Hugging Face
